title: Last Light — Orbital Salvage
description: A finished single-impulse orbital rescue desk. Three stranded spacecraft arrive on atmospheric-intersecting ellipses. Users choose a burn point on the orbit or time slider, shape a tangential/radial velocity impulse, and replay the altered future. A recovery line, first-entry deadline, true perigee/apogee forecast, repair assistant, custom incoming orbits, and selectable flight sheet make the orbital mechanics actionable.
concept: An industrial salvage workshop, arranged as an incoming dossier, an Earth-centered drafting table, an intervention console, and an alternate-ending replay tape. The mission is to rescue a complete orbit above a geometric recovery altitude with one ideal impulse.

exactFullRerunCommand: cd /workspace/scratch/bb2a48021f5a/planet-lab/experiments/orbital-mechanics/astra-xhigh-bold && node --check physics.js && node --check main.js && node numerical-tests.mjs > numerical-results.json && node verify-build.mjs > build-results.json
numericalAssumptions: Earth gravitational parameter μ = 398600.4418 km³/s²; spherical radius = 6371 km.
Massless point spacecraft in an inertial 2D plane under central Newtonian gravity.
Universal-variable Kepler propagation with safeguarded Newton/bisection solve and Stumpff functions; bound periods reduced modulo the orbital period.
One instantaneous velocity impulse; tangential is perpendicular to the radius in the current direction of angular motion; radial is outward.
Burn components limited to ±1500 m/s; impulse cost is the Euclidean norm, not a propellant estimate.
The first future inbound 120 km altitude crossing is a terminal operational boundary. Event times from conic anomalies are refined against the actual propagator.
Recovery means a bound orbit whose perigee reaches the selected recovery altitude, with a 1e-6 km floating-point comparison tolerance.

The assisted rescue is an apogee tangent impulse targeted to the recovery perigee, for below-target incoming ellipses with a reachable apogee; already-safe incoming orbits receive a zero-cost no-burn recommendation.
Replay ends at the first air crossing or the coast horizon, whichever comes first: one post-burn orbit capped at 8 hours for bound trajectories, 2 hours for open trajectories.
Orbital path and Earth geometry share one physical scale; spacecraft, markers, labels, and impulse arrows are magnified for usability.
limitations: No atmosphere, drag, heating, breakup, landing, oblateness/J₂, third bodies, solar pressure, 3D inclination changes, finite burns, pointing/fuel/mass constraints, or real celestial data.
A geometric recovery line is not a real-flight safety guarantee; real atmospheric decay can occur above 120 km.
The minimum-cost assistant is scoped to lifting a low perigee from a reachable apogee. It does not solve arbitrary multi-burn optimization.
Numerical tests establish ideal-model consistency, not real-mission accuracy.
Flight sheets are selectable in-memory text. There is no persistent storage, account system, backend, or external sharing.

repairs.issue: A near-parabolic probe showed an atmospheric crossing radius residual of approximately 0.000723309 km for one near-escape ellipse and approximately 0.0000161282 km for adjacent near-parabolic cases.
repairs.change: Added event-time Newton refinement against the actual universal-variable propagator and seven near-parabolic regression tests.
repairs.verifiedResult: All seven crossing residuals are ≤1.819e-12 km, below the 1e-6 km test tolerance.

repairs.issue: Already-safe custom incoming orbits should not spend delta-v to lower their perigee to the requested recovery line.
repairs.change: The repair assistant now returns the zero-burn solution and explains that the incoming orbit is already clear.
repairs.verifiedResult: Source-level repair; browser interaction not verified.

repairs.issue: A distant future atmospheric return could otherwise extend replay past the declared coast horizon.
repairs.change: Replay duration now takes the minimum of first-entry time and the bounded post-burn coast duration, with an explicit endsAtEntry flag and accurate terminal labels.
repairs.verifiedResult: Replay cap and boundary regression tests pass.
